HudElement, Named
public final class ExampleClock extends AbstractHudElement
A HUD element with settings and a rounded, non-rectangular hit region.

Shows three things a real element needs:

  • Settings by declaration. Extending AbstractHudElement brings in SettingHolder, so the fields below register and persist themselves alongside the layout.
  • A size that changes every frame. The text is wider with seconds on than off, and the anchor formula moves the element the right way when it changes.
  • A frozen sample while editing. isEditing() keeps the box from resizing under the cursor as the clock ticks.

    • getPreferredSize

      public Size getPreferredSize()
      Description copied from interface: HudElement
      Current natural size.

      Expected to differ every frame. A clock is wider at 12:00 than 1:00, an ArrayList grows as modules are toggled. Nothing caches this, and the anchor formula makes a size change move the element in the right direction on its own.

    • render

      public void render(float x, float y, float w, float h)
      Description copied from interface: HudElement
      Draws the element with its top-left corner at (x, y).

      w and h are the natural size reported by HudElement.getPreferredSize() this frame, not the scaled size: any scale factor is already applied as a transform around this call.

    • getShape

      public Shape getShape(float x, float y, float w, float h)
      The drawn shape is a rounded rectangle, so the hit region should be too. Clicking the very corner of a rounded panel ought to miss it.
